code: truth   <- attr(static_assay, "truth") Tr      <- unique(long$Tr) tau_ref <- unique(long$tau_ref) mass    <- c(10, 20)  log_a <- truth$log_a + truth$b_mass * (mass - 15) simulated <- c(   # a at the reference temperature and time of the fitted model   exp(log_a + truth$b * (Tr - truth$T_ref)) * (tau_ref / truth$scale)^truth$shape,   truth$b, truth$shape, truth$shape * log(10) / truth$b,   # sCTmax for p = 0.5 and 60 min: the temperature at which M(T) H0(60) = log(2)   truth$T_ref + (log(log(2)) - log_a - truth$shape * log(60 / truth$scale)) / truth$b )  keep <- c("median", "lower", "upper") estimated <- rbind(   tol$params[tol$params$quantity == "a", keep],   tol$params[tol$params$mass == 10 & tol$params$quantity != "a", keep],   tol$sctmax[tol$sctmax$p == 0.5, keep] ) comparison <- data.frame(   quantity  = c("a (10 g)", "a (20 g)", "b", "k", "z", "sCTmax (10 g)", "sCTmax (20 g)"),   simulated = simulated,   estimated ) knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)

code: truth   <- attr(ramp_assay, "truth") Tr      <- unique(long$Tr) tau_ref <- unique(long$tau_ref)  # The temperature at which half of the fish have failed under a ramp from 14°C. simulated_dctmax <- function(rate, T_start = 14, p = 0.5) {   hazard <- function(t) {     exp(truth$log_a + truth$b * (T_start + rate * t - truth$T_ref)) *       (truth$shape / truth$scale) * (t / truth$scale)^(truth$shape - 1)   }   accrued <- function(t) integrate(hazard, lower = 0, upper = t)$value + log(1 - p)   T_start + rate * uniroot(accrued, interval = c(1, 20 / rate), tol = 1e-8)$root }  simulated <- c(   # a at the reference temperature and time of the fitted model   exp(truth$log_a + truth$b * (Tr - truth$T_ref)) * (tau_ref / truth$scale)^truth$shape,   truth$b, truth$shape, truth$shape * log(10) / truth$b,   # sCTmax for p = 0.5 and 60 min: the temperature at which M(T) H0(60) = log(2)   truth$T_ref + (log(log(2)) - truth$log_a - truth$shape * log(60 / truth$scale)) / truth$b,   vapply(rates, simulated_dctmax, numeric(1)) )  keep <- c("median", "lower", "upper") comparison <- data.frame(   quantity  = c("a", "b", "k", "z", "sCTmax (60 min)",                 paste0("dCTmax (", rates, "°C per min)")),   simulated = simulated,   rbind(tol$params[keep], tol$sctmax[tol$sctmax$p == 0.5, keep], dct[keep]) ) knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)

code: rates_wide <- c(0.025, 0.1, 0.3) ramp_wide  <- subset(ramp_assay, do == 10 & rate %in% rates_wide) path_wide  <- ramp_path(c("r0.025", "r0.1", "r0.3"), T_start = 14, rate = rates_wide,                         t_max = 15.5 / rates_wide) long_wide  <- build_hazard_data(ramp_wide, path_wide, observation = "continuous",                                 covariates = c("mass", "trial")) fit_wide   <- fit_hazard(   long_wide,   m_form        = "exp",   baseline      = "weibull",   dpar_formulas = formulas,   chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, cores = 4, seed = 20261006,   control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95), backend = "cmdstanr" ) pred      <- predict_survival(fit, stream_record, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15)) pred_wide <- predict_survival(fit_wide, stream_record, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15)) # Survival under the model used to simulate the data, with the hazard accrued # between consecutive readings taken at the temperature midway between them. truth    <- attr(ramp_assay, "truth") n        <- nrow(stream_record) midpoint <- (stream_record$temp[-1] + stream_record$temp[-n]) / 2 accrued  <- exp(truth$log_a + truth$b * (midpoint - truth$T_ref)) *   diff((stream_record$time / truth$scale)^truth$shape) simulated_survival <- data.frame(time = stream_record$time,                                  survival = c(1, exp(-cumsum(accrued)))) # pred_static is the prediction of the vignette Getting started with rTFT (there, pred) panels <- c("Stream temperature (°C)",             "Survival: static assay",             "Survival: ramps at 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3°C per min (3-fold span)",             "Survival: ramps at 0.025, 0.1 and 0.3°C per min (12-fold span)") temperature <- data.frame(panel = panels[1], time = stream_record$time,                           temp = stream_record$temp) predicted <- rbind(   data.frame(panel = panels[2], pred_static$survival),   data.frame(panel = panels[3], pred$survival),   data.frame(panel = panels[4], pred_wide$survival) )  # Survival under the model used to simulate the data is drawn in each of the three # panels of survival. simulated_survival <- merge(data.frame(panel = panels[2:4]), simulated_survival)  # The three panels of survival share an axis from 0 to 1. axis_ends <- data.frame(panel = rep(panels[2:4], each = 2), time = 0, survival = c(0, 1))  # The panels share one order in the four tables. temperature$panel        <- factor(temperature$panel, levels = panels) predicted$panel          <- factor(predicted$panel, levels = panels) simulated_survival$panel <- factor(simulated_survival$panel, levels = panels) axis_ends$panel          <- factor(axis_ends$panel, levels = panels)  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = time / 1440)) +   geom_blank(data = axis_ends, aes(y = survival)) +   geom_line(data = temperature, aes(y = temp), colour = "grey20") +   geom_ribbon(data = predicted, aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),               fill = "#225EA8", alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line(data = predicted, aes(y = median), colour = "#225EA8") +   geom_line(data = simulated_survival, aes(y = survival), linetype = "dashed",             colour = "grey20") +   facet_wrap(vars(panel), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   labs(x = "Time (days)", y = NULL) +   theme_light() coverage <- rbind(pred$coverage, pred_wide$coverage) knitr::kable(data.frame(   `Ramp rates (°C per min)` = c("0.1, 0.2, 0.3", "0.025, 0.1, 0.3"),   coverage[c("Ta_failed_min", "Ta_failed_max", "below", "risk_below",              "tau_max", "beyond", "risk_beyond")],   check.names = FALSE ), digits = 2) heat_wave      <- subset(stream_record, day %in% 16:20) heat_wave$time <- heat_wave$time - heat_wave$time[1] predict_survival(fit, heat_wave, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15))$mortality

text: Three simulated datasets included package: static assay (static_assay), ramping assay run two levels dissolved oxygen (ramp_assay) record stream temperature (stream_record). simulated known model, model estimates can compared values used simulation. example uses static_assay, contains times loss equilibrium 120 juvenile salmonids held 23, 25 27°C checked every hour five days. shows four steps analysis, vignette Getting started rTFT describes detail.
code: library(rTFT)  # 1. The table of intervals at risk, built from the temperature of each group of #    fish through time and the times of the checks. path   <- data.frame(path_id = rep(c("T23", "T25", "T27"), each = 2),                      time    = rep(c(0, 7200), times = 3),                      temp    = rep(c(23, 25, 27), each = 2)) checks <- expand.grid(path_id = c("T23", "T25", "T27"), time = seq(0, 7200, by = 60)) long   <- build_hazard_data(static_assay, path, observation = "interval",                             covariates = c("mass", "trial"), checks = checks)  # 2. An exponential failure rate with a Weibull baseline, with the failure rate #    depending on body mass and varying among trials. fit <- fit_hazard(long, m_form = "exp", baseline = "weibull",                   dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + I(mass - 15) + (1 | trial)),                   chains = 4, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr")  # 3. The static critical thermal maximum for an exposure of 60 min and the thermal #    death time curves of a 15 g fish. tol <- derive_tdt_ttl(fit, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15), t_ref = 60) tol$sctmax plot_tdt(tol, time_unit = "min")  # 4. Survival along 30 days of hourly stream temperature. pred <- predict_survival(fit, stream_record, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15)) plot_survival(pred, temperature = TRUE)

log(tau_ref) + (exp(logshape) - 1) * (log_tau - log(tau_ref)) + loga + exp(logb) * (Ta - Tc) - log1p(exp(-50 * (Ta - Tc))) + log_exposure  #> loga ~ 1 #> logb ~ 1 #> Tc ~ 1 #> logshape ~ 1 #>  #> $family #>  #> Custom family: cloglog_bern  #> Link function: identity  #> Parameters: mu  #>  #>  #> $observation #> [1] "interval" #>   # A different structure per parameter: acclim as a fixed covariate on the # amplitude loga, and a trial-level random intercept on both loga and the # temperature sensitivity logb (`acclim` and `trial` are carried through by # build_hazard_data()). build_hazard_spec("exp",   dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + acclim + (1 | trial), logb = ~ 1 + (1 | trial))) #> $formula #> failed ~ loga + exp(logb) * (Ta - Tr) + log_exposure  #> loga ~ 1 + acclim + (1 | trial) #> logb ~ 1 + (1 | trial) #>  #> $family #>  #> Custom family: cloglog_bern  #> Link function: identity  #> Parameters: mu  #>  #>  #> $observation #> [1] "interval" #>   # Mixed interval-censored and known-time failures: the response holds the per-row # `exact` flag through vint(). build_hazard_spec("exp", observation = "mixed") #> $formula #> failed | vint(exact) ~ loga + exp(logb) * (Ta - Failures at a known time are also given a #>   short closing interval, so their hazard is that of the moment of failure. #> ℹ Set `grid_dT` to change the step, or to `Inf` to keep the intervals as given. models <- build_hazard_models("exp", c("mem", "weibull"),                               dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + (1 | trial)))  # the bundle, written into a temporary folder here; rtft_source says the cluster # installs rTFT from its repository on GitHub (by default it is read from how rTFT # was installed on this machine) bundle <- file.path(tempdir(), "my-run") write_hpc_bundle(models, long, bundle, account = "def-someone", kfold = TRUE,                  remote = "someone@nibi.alliancecan.ca:scratch/my-run",                  rtft_source = "eogmartins/rTFT", chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 1) #> ℹ Leaving out one trial at a time: the individuals of each trial share its #>   effect in the model, so leaving out one individual would leave that effect in #>   the fit. #> ℹ Use `unit = "id"` to leave out individuals instead. #> ✔ Wrote a bundle of 2 models to /tmp/Rtmp48sKkX/my-run: 2 fits and 4 refits for #>   cross-validation, leaving out one trial at a time. #> ℹ Copy it to the cluster with the command in step 1 of README.txt, in that #>   folder. #> ℹ Then, on the cluster, in that folder, run these two (the first once on each #>   cluster): #>   bash install.sh #>   bash check.sh list.files(bundle, recursive = TRUE) #>  [1] "README.txt"             "check.sh"               "inputs/checksums.txt"   #>  [4] "inputs/data.rds"        "inputs/models.rds"      "inputs/settings.rds"    #>  [7] "inputs/tasks-fit.csv"   "inputs/tasks-kfold.csv" "install.R"              #> [10] "install.sh"             "settings.sh"            "status.sh"              #> [13] "submit.sh"              "task.sh"
